proposed_comments.title: Keep wheel interception isolated and consistent

confidence.rationale: The hook is enabled by either mouse feature, but the current callbacks share state and accumulate deltas before proving wheel switching is active. This deterministically changes disabled right/middle-button behavior and leaks or loses partial high-resolution gestures.

proposed_comments.body:
### Keep wheel interception isolated and consistent

**Severity:** `high`

Enabling mouse-wheel layout switching also activates the existing right/X-button hook path even when the non-primary mouse-button setting is off. Separately, partial high-resolution deltas are accumulated while switching is inactive and forwarded before a later packet is consumed, so a gesture can both scroll the target and switch layouts. Gate the right/middle callbacks by their own settings, expose a direction-aware `can switch` predicate to the hook, clear inactive/reversed/disabled accumulation, and reserve the complete high-resolution gesture only while a valid switch is available.

proposed_comments.title: Revalidate queued switches and de-duplicate layout IDs

confidence.rationale: The switch is posted asynchronously without checking the API result or revalidating drag/settings state. Duplicate UUIDs under multiple hotkeys also make a two-entry cycle that reapplies the current layout while consuming input.

proposed_comments.body:
### Revalidate queued switches and de-duplicate layout IDs

**Severity:** `high`

`PostMessageW` failure currently still reports the wheel as handled, and the queued handler can apply and persist a layout after the drag ended or the setting was disabled. Return the post result and recheck the active drag, setting, work area, and next layout in the message handler. Also de-duplicate valid quick-layout UUIDs in hotkey order before deciding that at least two layouts can be cycled; otherwise two keys mapped to one layout consume scrolling without changing anything.

proposed_comments.title: Keep the label and drag highlight synchronized with the new layout

confidence.rationale: The overlay render loop ends with the shorter scene animation and hidden overlays still accept labels. RefreshLayouts also clears drawing without resetting the snapper's cached highlighted-zone indices.

proposed_comments.body:
### Keep the label and drag highlight synchronized with the new layout

**Severity:** `medium`

The layout-name label can be stored while the overlay is hidden, while a visible label configured for longer than the flash animation is cleared when that shorter animation ends. Keep rendering until both lifetimes expire and ignore label requests unless the overlay is already visible. After applying a layout during a drag, reset the snapper's cached highlighted-zone state before recomputing at the cursor; otherwise the same-numbered zone or a multi-zone anchor can remain visually stale. The settings description should also cover switching whenever zones are visible, not only while dragging.
